differences.what: Fabrication types: old {nothing, nothing} per user pair (2 entries per pair, per face); current {edge_insertion, edge_insertion} per face. The plate merge keys on the marker polyline size (old wood_element.cpp joint line = outlines[1], current MergeModifier marker = (*outlines)[0][1].point_count()), so the type mostly affects exported output types, but it is a declared divergence.

Polyline structure: old emits each user polyline twice (per pair: [P_face0, P_face0] into face 0, [P_face1, P_face1] into face 1), N pairs → 2N polylines per face, untranslated, in the unit box; current emits one tiled outline per face (copies i=0..divisions-1, pair i % n_pairs, shifted along z by mv_end + mv_step*i) plus a 2-point front/back marker, i.e. 2 polylines per face, and multiple user pairs are cycled across the divisions instead of all emitted.

unit_scale: old leaves unit_scale=false (volumes stretched to the full edge); current sets unit_scale=true and uses divisions / joint_lines[0] / scale[2] / unit_scale_distance the ss_e_ip_2 way. Old had no divisions parameter at all; current factory adds divisions=4.

Source of the outlines: old global vectors GLOBALS::CUSTOM_JOINTS_SS_E_IP_MALE/FEMALE; current per-joint parameters.outlines routed through Settings::custom_joints["ss_e_ip"] (a rename of the channel, not of the joint).

In-plane volumes (:960-1001): d0 = half thickness of element 0, offset_plane_0/1 = Plane0[i] translated by ∓d0 along its normal (side face i of the male element), loopOfPlanes0 = {offset_0, Plane0[0] (top), offset_1, Plane0[1] (bottom)}, loopOfPlanes1 = {offset_0, Plane1[0], offset_1, Plane1[1]}; joint_volumes[0] = plane_4planes(plEnd0, loop0), [1] = plane_4planes(plEnd1, loop0), [2] = plane_4planes(plEnd0, loop1), [3] = plane_4planes(plEnd1, loop1); type = 12 (:1041). Rect point order from plane_4planes: p0 = offset_0∩top, p1 = top∩offset_1, p2 = offset_1∩bottom, p3 = bottom∩offset_0. Orientation (cmake/src/wood/include/wood_joint.cpp:270-355 orient_to_connection_area, change_basis :103-...): unit box origin (-0.5,-0.5,-0.5) → O0 = rect0[0]; unit X → X0 = rect0[1]-rect0[0] (across the edge, from the -d0 to the +d0 offset plane, i.e. the normal of the male's side face i, lying in the plate plane); unit Y → Y0 = rect0[3]-rect0[0] (top→bottom, plate thickness); unit Z → Z0 = rect1[0]-rect0[0] (along the joint line from plEnd0 to plEnd1). Male outlines (m[0], m[1]) take xform0 from volumes[0],[1]; female (f[0], f[1]) take xform1 from volumes[2],[3] (wood_joint.cpp:248-267, :343-357). With unit_scale the pair is slid to the midpoint then apart by unit_scale_distance along Z (:276-320). Therefore the insertion direction of every ss_e_ip joint (edge_insertion fingers spanning x in [-0.5,0.5]) is unit +X = the side-face normal of the male plate at the contact face (perpendicular to the shared edge, in the plate plane); a user insertion vector only tilts the end planes (skews Z), it does not change X. votes.reason: The finding is confirmed by the code; the difference changes the produced geometry. OLD: ss_e_ip_custom only copies the global custom polylines into m[0]/m[1]/f[0]/f[1] (each pair pushed twice, cut type nothing) and never touches unit_scale or divisions (351933c:wood_joint_lib.cpp:1547-1570); the struct default is unit_scale=false (351933c:wood_joint.h:85). The dispatcher sets unit_scale_distance and runs get_divisions for every joint (351933c:wood_joint_lib.cpp:6222-6223) but the custom builder ignores divisions, and the only other place that sets unit_scale for a custom joint is the XML read_xml path (351933c:wood_joint_lib.cpp:256), which is commented out at the id-9 call site (6315-6324) and is never called live (only commented references at 2957, 6322, 6384, 6441, 6482, 6548, 6559); wood_main.cpp has zero unit_scale mentions. With unit_scale=false, orient_to_connection_area skips the volume move (351933c:wood_joint.cpp:276-320) and change_basis maps the unit cube z-span onto the full distance between joint_volumes[0] and [1] (351933c:wood_joint.cpp:343-348), i.e. one custom tooth stretched over the whole edge. NEW: ss_e_ip_custom computes edge_length from joint_lines[0], clamps joint.divisions to [1,100], uses unit_scale_distance (fallback 40) and scale[2], tiles each custom face `divisions` times along z with mv_end/mv_step exactly as ss_e_ip_2, and sets unit_scale=true (ss_e_ip_custom.h:34-48, 54-85, 101); the factory adds divisions=4 (wood_element_joint_plate.h:58, .cpp:1009-1013) which compute_parameters copies into connection.divisions and sets unit_scale_distance=thickness for type 12 (wood_element_joint_plate.cpp:881-888); apply_unit_scale then slides the volume rectangles to unit_scale_distance apart before change of basis (wood_feature_construction.cpp:44-66, 91-98, 103-110). GEOMETRY for a concrete pair (two coplanar plates, thickness 40, shared edge 1000 mm, scale 1, custom male/female polylines with unit z in [-0.5,0.5]): old -> a single tooth whose z-extent is mapped to the 1000 mm edge (stretched 25x relative to thickness), count independent of divisions. New -> divisions=4: move_length_scaled=1000/(4*40)=6.25, total_length_scaled=25, mv_end=9.375, dz=+9.375,+3.125,-3.125,-9.375 unit; after unit_scale the unit cube z maps to 40 mm, so four 40-mm-long teeth centred at z=+375,+125,-125,-375 mm at 250-mm pitch (with 210 mm gaps between teeth). Point sets, polyline counts (old: one outline per face per pair; new: one concatenated outline plus one front-back line per face) and axial extents differ, so the claimed difference is real and visible. Side note outside the claim: old cut type is wood::cut::nothing (1557-1558, 1567-1568) while new is FabricationType::edge_insertion (ss_e_ip_custom.h:96-99).
